question: Which of the following schemes provide the highest discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The equivalent discount of two successive discounts x% and y% is approximately equal to their sum (x + y)% for comparison purposes.

Scheme 1: 10 + 3 = 13% | Scheme 2: 10 + 10 = 20%

Scheme 3: 7 + 10 = 17% | Scheme 4: 5 + 10 = 15%

Scheme 2 has the highest sum, thereby yielding the highest equivalent discount of 19%.

**∴ The correct answer is Two successive discounts of 10% each (19%).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme 1: 10% and 3%

Scheme 2: 10% and 10%

Scheme 3: 7% and 10%

Scheme 4: 5% and 10%

**Formula Used:**

Equivalent discount for two successive discounts x% and y% = (x + y − x × y / 100)%

 Effective Discount % Comparison
 10% and 3%
 
 12.7%
 10% and 10%
 
 19.0% (Highest)
 7% and 10%
 
 16.3%
 5% and 10%
 
 14.5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount for Scheme 1 = 10 + 3 − (10 × 3) / 100 = 13 − 0.3 = 12.7%

⇒ Discount for Scheme 2 = 10 + 10 − (10 × 10) / 100 = 20 − 1 = 19%

⇒ Discount for Scheme 3 = 7 + 10 − (7 × 10) / 100 = 17 − 0.7 = 16.3%

⇒ Discount for Scheme 4 = 5 + 10 − (5 × 10) / 100 = 15 − 0.5 = 14.5%

⇒ Scheme 2 provides the highest overall discount at 19%.

**∴ The correct answer is Two successive discounts of 10% each (19%).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts Formula

When two discounts of x% and y% are given consecutively, the overall effective discount is calculated using the formula (x + y − x × y / 100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

The final Selling Price (SP) after successive discounts d₁% and d₂% is determined as SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100).

Buy X Get Y Free

For promotional offers formatted as 'Buy X Get Y Free', the equivalent discount percentage is given by (Y ÷ (X + Y)) × 100%.
